_note: The documented wire contract between this server and the TOSCA-2 collab frontend. Every shape here is taken from the frontend's own guards in src/collab/stores/collabTracking.ts (isRawMarkerDictionary / isTrackingFeatureCollection / isCalibrationAck, parseRawMarkerSnapshot, buildMapCalibrationFromMarkerReadings) and from known_good_map_calibration_2026-08-31.json, the handshake the operator confirmed working on the live rig. Backend contract tests read this file rather than restating the JSON inline, so the two sides cannot drift apart silently.

map_calibration._note: points are ordered by MAP_CALIBRATION_MARKERS, i.e. 200, 201, 202, 203. lat_lon_position is [lat, lng]. Pixel positions below are the operator-confirmed 2026-08-31 readings.

clear_calibration._note: Drops the homography so the raw marker feed resumes; this is how the frontend re-enters calibration.

raw_marker_snapshot._note: Plain object keyed by marker id; each value is [pixel_x, pixel_y, rotation, camera_or_tag]. Sent while no basemap homography is configured. JSON object keys are strings; the frontend does Number(key), so numeric ids survive the round trip. An empty object is valid and means 'nothing on the table'.

building_geojson._note: Sent once a basemap homography exists. Only ids present in physical-building-catalog.json become features, so calibration markers 200-203 never appear here. An empty FeatureCollection is still a valid, meaningful message (it proves Python is on the calibrated feed).
